slides.title: Push-to-talk in ATAK
slides.html: OpenDefence Voice is push-to-talk (PTT) voice inside ATAK. Hold the PTT button and talk to your net, the voice channel you joined. The button turns red and reads TRANSMITTING while you are on the air. You hear the others, with the map still in front of you.

slides.title: Nothing to sign in to
slides.html: A separate voice app would mean a second sign-in and a second set of settings. OpenDefence Voice reuses what ATAK already holds, the TAK server's address and your certificate. It connects by itself and shows Connected, with nothing to sign in to.

slides.title: On the thumb bar
slides.html: OpenDefence Voice works on its own, opened from ATAK's ≡ menu. With OpenDefence Main in the same ATAK, it also gets a Voice button on the thumb bar, the row of buttons at the bottom left of the map. Push-to-talk is then one tap from the map.

slides.title: Works with the phone locked
slides.html: OpenDefence Voice keeps working with ATAK in the background and the phone locked. A Bluetooth PTT button, a headset's talk button or the volume-up key, once set up in Settings, lets you talk even then. The notification Voice push-to-talk is ready means they work now.
